671: static block gen_const_array(block expr) {
672:   /*
673:    * An expr of all constant elements looks like this:
674:    *
675:    * 0009 FORK 0027
676:    * 0011 FORK 0023
677:    * 0013 FORK 0019
678:    * 0015 LOADK 1
679:    * 0017 JUMP 0021
680:    * 0019 LOADK 2
681:    * 0021 JUMP 0025
682:    * 0023 LOADK 3
683:    * 0025 JUMP 0029
684:    * 0027 LOADK 4
685:    *
686:    * That's: N-1 commas for N elements, N LOADKs, and a JUMP between
687:    * every LOADK.  The sequence ends in a LOADK.  Any deviation and it's
688:    * not a list of constants.
689:    *
690:    * Here we check for this pattern almost exactly.  We don't check that
691:    * the targets of the FORK and JUMP instructions are in the right
692:    * sequence.
693:    */
694:   int all_const = 1;
695:   int commas = 0;
696:   int normal = 1;
697:   jv a = jv_array();
698:   for (inst *i = expr.first; i; i = i->next) {
699:     if (i->op == FORK) {
700:       commas++;
701:       if (i->imm.target == NULL || i->imm.target->op != JUMP ||
702:           jv_array_length(jv_copy(a)) > 0) {
703:         normal = 0;
704:         break;
705:       }
706:     } else if (all_const && i->op == LOADK) {
707:       if (i->next != NULL && i->next->op != JUMP) {
708:         normal = 0;
709:         break;
710:       }
711:       a = jv_array_append(a, jv_copy(i->imm.constant));
712:     } else if (i->op != JUMP || i->imm.target == NULL ||
713:                i->imm.target->op != LOADK) {
714:       all_const = 0;
715:     }
716:   }
717: 
718:   if (all_const && normal &&
719:       (expr.last == NULL || expr.last->op == LOADK) &&
720:       jv_array_length(jv_copy(a)) == commas + 1) {
721:     block_free(expr);
722:     return gen_const(a);
723:   }
724: 
725:   jv_free(a);
726:   block b = {0,0};
727:   return b;
728: }

776: /* Build wrappers around destructuring matchers so that we can chain them
777:  * when we have errors.  The approach is as follows:
778:  * DESTRUCTURE_ALT NEXT_MATCHER (unless last matcher)
779:  * existing_matcher_block
780:  * JUMP BODY
781:  */
782: static block bind_alternation_matchers(block matchers, block body) {
783:   block preamble = {0};
784:   block altmatchers = {0};
785:   block mb = {0};
786:   block final_matcher = matchers;
787: 
788:   // Pass through the matchers to find all destructured names.
789:   while (final_matcher.first && final_matcher.first->op == DESTRUCTURE_ALT) {
790:     block_append(&altmatchers, inst_block(block_take(&final_matcher)));
791:   }
792: 
793:   // We don't have any alternations here, so we can use the simplest case.
794:   if (altmatchers.first == NULL) {
795:     return bind_matcher(final_matcher, body);
796:   }
797: 
798:   // Collect var names
799:   jv all_vars = jv_object();
800:   block_get_unbound_vars(altmatchers, &all_vars);
801:   block_get_unbound_vars(final_matcher, &all_vars);
802: 
803:   // We need a preamble of STOREVs to which to bind the matchers and the body.
804:   jv_object_keys_foreach(all_vars, key) {
805:     preamble = BLOCK(preamble,
806:                      gen_op_simple(DUP),
807:                      gen_const(jv_null()),
808:                      gen_op_unbound(STOREV, jv_string_value(key)));
809:     jv_free(key);
810:   }
811:   jv_free(all_vars);
812: 
813:   // Now we build each matcher in turn
814:   for (inst *i = altmatchers.first; i; i = i->next) {
815:     block submatcher = i->subfn;
816: 
817:     // If we're successful, jump to the end of the matchers
818:     submatcher = BLOCK(submatcher, gen_op_target(JUMP, final_matcher));
819: 
820:     // DESTRUCTURE_ALT to the end of this submatcher so we can skip to the next one on error
821:     mb = BLOCK(mb, gen_op_target(DESTRUCTURE_ALT, submatcher), submatcher);
822: 
823:     // We're done with this inst and we don't want it anymore
824:     // But we can't let it free the submatcher block.
825:     i->subfn.first = i->subfn.last = NULL;
826:   }
827:   // We're done with these insts now.
828:   block_free(altmatchers);
829: 
830:   return bind_matcher(preamble, BLOCK(mb, final_matcher, body));
831: }

850: block gen_foreach(block source, block matcher, block init, block update, block extract) {
851:   block output = gen_op_targetlater(JUMP);
852:   block state_var = gen_op_var_fresh(STOREV, "foreach");
853:   block loop = BLOCK(gen_op_simple(DUPN),
854:                      // get a value from the source expression:

857:                      // in the body to see

861:                                         // generate updated state

864:                                         gen_op_simple(DUP),
865:                                         // save new state
866:                                         gen_op_bound(STOREV, state_var),
867:                                         // extract an output...
868:                                         extract,
869:                                         // ...and output it by jumping
870:                                         // past the BACKTRACK that comes
871:                                         // right after the loop body,
872:                                         // which in turn is there
873:                                         // because...
874:                                         //
875:                                         // (Incidentally, extract can also
876:                                         // backtrack, e.g., if it calls

879:                                         output)));

882:                         state_var,

Rename the FORK\_OPT opcode to TRY\_BEGIN, add a TRY\_END opcode, and wrap errors when raising through a TRY\_END so that they will not be caught by the matching TRY\_BEGIN.

Now a `try exp catch handler` expression generates code like:

```
TRY_BEGIN handler
<exp>
TRY_END
JUMP past_handler
handler: <handler>
past_handler:
...
```

On backtrack through TRY\_BEGIN it just backtracks.

If anything past the whole thing raises when produced a value, then the TRY\_END will catch the error, wrap it in another, and backtrack. The TRY\_BEGIN will see a wrapped error and then it will unwrap and re-raise the error.

If raises, then TRY\_BEGIN will catch the error and jump to the handler, but the TRY\_BEGIN will not stack\_save() in that case, so on raise/backtrack the TRY\_BEGIN will not execute again (nor will the TRY\_END).

block gen_try(block exp, block handler) {
  /*
   * Produce:
   *
   *  TRY_BEGIN handler
   *  <exp>
   *  TRY_END
   *  JUMP past_handler
   *  handler: <handler>
   *  past_handler:
   *
   * If <exp> backtracks then TRY_BEGIN will backtrack.
   *
   * If <exp> produces a value then we'll execute whatever bytecode follows
   * this sequence.  If that code raises an exception, then TRY_END will wrap
   * and re-raise that exception, and TRY_BEGIN will unwrap and re-raise the
   * exception (see jq_next()).
   *
   * If <exp> raises then the TRY_BEGIN will see a non-wrapped exception and

part.text:
The fix is complete and validated. Summary:

**Root cause:** A `try` body compiled to a `FORK_OPT` forkpoint that was never discarded after the try body succeeded. When a later error (from a piped expression or the second try's handler) backtracked through that stale forkpoint, the first try's catch handler incorrectly ran.

**Fix (mirrors upstream jq PR #2750):**
- `src/opcode_list.h`: renamed `FORK_OPT` → `TRY_BEGIN`, added a new `TRY_END` opcode.
- `src/compile.c` / `src/compile.h`: removed `gen_try_handler`; `gen_try` now emits `TRY_BEGIN handler; <exp>; TRY_END; JUMP past_handler; handler: ...`.
- `src/execute.c`: `TRY_END` wraps errors raised after the try body produced a value; `ON_BACKTRACK(TRY_BEGIN)` unwraps and re-raises those instead of catching them, and only jumps to the handler for unwrapped (body-raised) errors.
- `src/parser.y` / `src/parser.c`: `try Exp catch Exp` now calls `gen_try($2, $4)` directly.

**Validation:** `make check` in the container passes all 8 suites (including the try/catch cases in `tests/jq.test`), and the issue repro now produces `["catch-b","error-b"]` instead of `["catch-a",["catch-b","error-b"]]`, matching the expected behavior.
